answer: Staked curation ties each new identity to a curator's own money. A curator stakes 50 credits and paints one pigment seal on its record; a fake costs the curator 50. A failed audit sends a ripple through that curator's book, re-checking every identity they endorsed. Repeated failures send the curator into a downward spiral, cutting future fees to zero. The k-th fake still needs a fresh 50-credit stake, so 1,000 fakes risk 50,000 credits, while an honest applicant needs one seal. Rented curators fail too: the first audit burns their stake, so rental cannot be reused.
